problem: The same letter C is used for two different things: capacitance in farads and the unit of charge, coulombs (C). A student reading 'Q is charge in coulombs (C) ... and C is capacitance in farads (F)' can confuse the symbol with the unit.
fix: Write: 'Q is charge in coulombs (unit symbol C), V is voltage in volts (V), and C is capacitance in farads (unit symbol F).' Or use q for charge throughout.

problem: 'Activation overpotential is extra voltage to start the electrode reactions' is loose. Activation overpotential is the extra voltage needed to drive the charge-transfer step at the required current; it exists even when the reaction is already running.
fix: 'Activation overpotential is the extra voltage needed to drive the charge-transfer reaction at the electrodes at the current drawn. It comes from the activation energy of the reaction.'

problem: Standard conditions for E° are stated as 25 °C and 1 bar only. The standard potential also requires unit activity (about 1 M) for dissolved species; without this a student may think pressure and temperature alone fix E°.
fix: 'E° is the standard cell potential at 25 °C, 1 bar for gases, and unit activity (about 1 M) for dissolved species.'

problem: P = V²/(4R) is presented as 'maximum power' without saying when it applies. It is the power delivered only when the load resistance equals the equivalent series resistance; a student may use it as the power for any load.
fix: Add: 'This is the largest power the device can deliver, reached when the load resistance equals R (the equivalent series resistance).'
